grammarFocus: 主题句与支持句；although / while；because 与 because of。
title: Why Schools Should Teach Financial Literacy
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，回答10个问题。文章和题目均为模拟练习材料，不是官方雅思试题。请先通读全文，再作答。答案必须来自原文。
passage:
A
In many countries, students learn mathematics and history, but they often do not learn how to manage money. This is a serious problem. Although young people use money every day, many of them do not know how to save, budget, or avoid debt. For example, a recent survey in a simulated study found that 60% of university students had no monthly budget. Because of this, they often spent more than they earned. Schools should teach financial literacy because it is a basic life skill. A person who understands money can make better decisions and feel less stress. In addition, financial literacy helps people plan for emergencies and avoid unnecessary borrowing. When students learn to manage money early, they are more likely to develop healthy financial habits that last a lifetime. These habits include saving regularly, comparing prices before buying, and understanding the difference between needs and wants. Such skills are not only useful for individuals but also benefit society as a whole, because financially responsible citizens contribute to a stable economy.

B
Some teachers argue that financial education belongs to parents, not schools. While this is a reasonable point, it is not a complete solution. Many parents do not have enough financial knowledge themselves. Because they never learned about money at school, they cannot teach their children. In addition, some families do not talk about money openly. As a result, children from these families may grow up without any financial guidance. Schools can provide equal opportunities for all students, while parents can support learning at home. For instance, a school in a simulated project in Shanghai introduced a weekly money club. Students learned to track their spending and set savings goals. Teachers reported that students became more careful with their pocket money. Parents also joined monthly workshops to learn how to discuss money at home. This shows that schools and families can work together effectively. Furthermore, when parents and teachers share the same message about money, students are more likely to take the lessons seriously. The money club also invited local bank staff to give simple talks about saving and borrowing. These talks helped students understand real-world financial products without promoting any specific company.

C
A financial literacy course does not need to be long or complex. It can be a short unit in a math or social studies class. Students can learn how to make a simple budget, how to compare prices, and how to save for a goal. They can also learn about the dangers of borrowing money without a plan. Although some people worry that this takes time away from other subjects, the benefits are clear. Students who learn these skills are less likely to have money problems later in life. Because financial habits form early, teaching these skills in school is a smart investment. Moreover, financial education can be integrated into existing subjects without adding extra hours. For example, math lessons can include real-life problems about saving and spending. Social studies classes can discuss how advertising influences buying decisions. In this way, students practice financial skills while they learn other content. Teachers do not need special textbooks; they can use everyday examples such as shopping lists and phone bills. This makes the lessons practical and easy to understand. Even a few hours of focused teaching can make a difference, as long as the content is relevant to students' daily lives.

D
In conclusion, financial literacy is essential for modern life. While schools already teach many important subjects, they should also teach students how to manage money. Because of the growing complexity of personal finance, young people need this knowledge more than ever. Schools and parents should work together to help students build a secure financial future. By starting early, we can prepare young people to make wise financial choices throughout their lives. It is also important for schools to review their financial education programs regularly to ensure they meet students' needs. With the right support, every student can gain the skills needed to manage money confidently.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Schools should teach students how to manage money.
Parents should not talk about money with their children.
Mathematics is more important than history.
University students spend too much money on books.
answers: Schools should teach students how to manage money.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段提出学校应该教授理财知识，后文围绕这一观点展开论证，因此主旨是学校应教学生理财。
questions.evidence: Schools should teach financial literacy because it is a basic life skill.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what percentage of university students had no monthly budget in the simulated study?
questions.explanation: 原文明确提到模拟研究中60%的大学生没有月度预算。
questions.evidence: a recent survey in a simulated study found that 60% of university students had no monthly budget.

questions.prompt: Why does the author say parents cannot always teach financial skills?
options: Because many parents lack financial knowledge themselves.
Because parents are too busy with work.
Because children do not listen to parents.
Because schools do not allow parents to teach.
answers: Because many parents lack financial knowledge themselves.
questions.explanation: 第二段指出许多家长自己缺乏理财知识，因此无法教孩子。
questions.evidence: Many parents do not have enough financial knowledge themselves.

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest about the length of a financial literacy course?
options: It can be a short unit in a math or social studies class.
It must be a full-year course.
It should be taught only at university.
It should replace history classes.
answers: It can be a short unit in a math or social studies class.
questions.explanation: 第三段提到理财课程不需要很长或很复杂，可以是数学或社会研究课中的一个短单元。
questions.evidence: It can be a short unit in a math or social studies class.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a skill students can learn in a financial course?
options: How to invest in the stock market
How to make a simple budget
How to compare prices
How to save for a goal
answers: How to invest in the stock market
questions.explanation: 原文提到学生可以学习制定简单预算、比较价格、为目标准蓄，但没有提到投资股票市场。
questions.evidence: Students can learn how to make a simple budget, how to compare prices, and how to save for a goal.

questions.prompt: The word 'investment' in the last sentence of paragraph C is closest in meaning to:
options: a wise use of time and resources
a large amount of money
a difficult exam
a type of bank account
answers: a wise use of time and resources
questions.explanation: 原文说“teaching these skills in school is a smart investment”，这里投资是比喻，指明智地利用时间和资源。
questions.evidence: teaching these skills in school is a smart investment.

questions.prompt: What is the author's conclusion about financial literacy?
options: It is essential for modern life and schools should teach it.
It is only important for rich people.
It should be taught only by parents.
It is too complex for schools to teach.
answers: It is essential for modern life and schools should teach it.
questions.explanation: 最后一段总结理财对现代生活至关重要，学校应教授，且家长和学校应合作。
questions.evidence: In conclusion, financial literacy is essential for modern life.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: 'Because financial habits form _____, teaching these skills in school is a smart investment.'
questions.explanation: 原文第三段最后一句说“Because financial habits form early”，因此填early。
questions.evidence: Because financial habits form early, teaching these skills in school is a smart investment.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The passage states that all parents talk openly about money with their children.
options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: 原文说“some families do not talk about money openly”，与“所有家长都公开谈钱”矛盾，因此是False。
questions.evidence: some families do not talk about money openly.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The passage mentions that financial education can reduce stress.
options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: 第一段最后一句说“A person who understands money can make better decisions and feel less stress”，因此是True。
questions.evidence: A person who understands money can make better decisions and feel less stress.

grammar.title: 主题句与支持句；although / while；because 与 because of
grammar.explanation: 主题句表达段落中心思想，支持句用例子、原因等支撑主题句。although 和 while 表示让步或对比，后接完整句子；because 后接句子，because of 后接名词或名词短语。
grammar.example: Although young people use money every day, many of them do not know how to save. Because of this, they often spent more than they earned.

options: Although it was raining, they went for a walk.
Although it was raining, but they went for a walk.
Although the rain, they went for a walk.
Although it was raining, they went for a walk because of.
answers: Although it was raining, they went for a walk.
questions.explanation: although 引导让步状语从句，后面接完整句子，主句前不加but。
questions.evidence: Although young people use money every day, many of them do not know how to save.

options: She stayed home because of the bad weather.
She stayed home because the bad weather.
She stayed home because of it was bad weather.
She stayed home because the weather bad.
answers: She stayed home because of the bad weather.
questions.explanation: because of 后接名词短语 the bad weather；because 后接句子。
questions.evidence: Because of this, they often spent more than they earned.

options: While I was reading, my brother was watching TV.
While I was reading, but my brother was watching TV.
While I was reading, my brother watching TV.
While reading, my brother was watching TV.
answers: While I was reading, my brother was watching TV.
questions.explanation: while 表示两个动作同时进行，后接完整句子，主句前不加but。
questions.evidence: While this is a reasonable point, it is not a complete solution.

options: He passed the exam because he studied hard.
He passed the exam because of he studied hard.
He passed the exam because his hard study.
He passed the exam because of studied hard.
answers: He passed the exam because he studied hard.
questions.explanation: because 后接完整句子 he studied hard；because of 后接名词短语。
